discovery: Quantum simulation of Hubbard models with ultracold atoms in optical lattices, from the superfluid-Mott insulator transition to single-site-resolved quantum gas microscopy

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and LMU Munich, Germany

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum many-body physics
motivation: Zoller's theoretical proposal (1998) showed that ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise the Bose-Hubbard model with tunable parameters. Bloch and Greiner's observation of the quantum phase transition from a superfluid to a Mott insulator (2002) made a textbook model of strongly correlated matter real and controllable, and founded analog quantum simulation. Both then developed quantum gas microscopes that image and address single atoms at single lattice sites. These instruments revealed Mott shells, antiferromagnetic order and string correlations in the Fermi-Hubbard model, entanglement entropy and many-body localisation. The work turned an idea of Feynman into an experimental discipline that connects atomic physics, condensed matter and quantum information. It underpins today's neutral-atom quantum simulators and quantum computers. It is a conceptual and technical breakthrough of lasting importance.
